name: Desmoplastic Infantile Astrocytoma/Ganglioglioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System (2021)

criteria.description: Presence of desmoplastic stroma with astrocytic and/or gangliogliomatous tumor cells
Tumor presenting in infants typically under 2 years of age
Large cystic and solid supratentorial mass with contrast enhancement on MRI
Absence of BRAF V600E mutation differentiating from other pediatric gliomas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of desmoplastic stroma with astrocytic/gangliogliomatous cells in an infant under 2 years presenting with characteristic imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing may aid in differential diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents as a large cystic and solid tumor causing mass effect
searchTerms: rapidly enlarging brain tumor in upper brain

pathognomonic.notes: Common initial presentation due to cortical irritation
searchTerms: convulsions due to outer brain involvement

pathognomonic.symptomName: Macrocephaly due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: large head from high brain pressure
head enlargement due to fluid buildup

common.notes: May occur secondary to tumor mass effect

common.symptomName: Vomiting due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: throwing up due to increased intracranial pressure

common.notes: Non-specific but common in infants with brain tumors

searchTerms: weakness on one side of body

occasional.symptomName: Visual disturbances due to optic pathway involvement
occasional.notes: May include nystagmus or decreased visual tracking
searchTerms: vision problems from optic nerve damage
blurred or lost vision due to optic pathway
neck muscle spasm causing head tilt

occasional.notes: Due to obstruction of CSF pathways
May be related to increased intracranial pressure or tumor location

rare.symptomName: Endocrine abnormalities due to hypothalamic involvement
rare.notes: Rare but possible if tumor invades hypothalamic region
searchTerms: endocrine dysfunction due to brain area damage
abnormal hormone levels from hypothalamic issues

laboratory: Generally nonspecific; routine labs usually normal
imaging: MRI showing large supratentorial cystic and solid mass with strong contrast enhancement
Mass effect with midline shift and possible hydrocephalus
other: Histopathology showing desmoplastic stroma with astrocytic and gangliogliomatous components
Immunohistochemistry positive for GFAP and neuronal markers

distinguishingFeatures: Different molecular profile including frequent BRAF alterations
Occurs in older children and young adults
Histology shows pleomorphic astrocytic cells without desmoplasia

redFlags: Rapid increase in head circumference in infant
New onset focal seizures in infant
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as vomiting and lethargy
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Desmoplastic Infantile Astrocytoma and Ganglioglioma. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases, 2020.
Pediatric Brain Tumors: Diagnosis and Treatment. Pediatric Neurology, 2019.
